result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.alpha_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get alpha centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L15860-L15973){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.alpha_centrality( alpha=0.1, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Alpha centrality is a generalization of eigenvector centrality that adds an exogenous factor: `x = α · A · x + e` where `α` is the attenuation factor, `A` is the adjacency matrix, and `e` is the exogenous factor (set to `1` for all nodes). Lower `α` emphasizes local neighborhood structure, while higher `α` considers more global structure. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.1]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Attenuation factor (range: `0` to `1`). Controls the balance between local and global structure. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations for convergence. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance threshold. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, auto-generates name from method name (`alpha_centrality`). [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns dictionary of results. If `False`, stores results as node attributes and returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to centrality scores. If `return_dict=` is `False`: returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Lower `alpha=` values keep the focus on a node's immediate neighborhood, while higher values let influence propagate further through the network -- both are shown here on the same star graph: ::: {#1af1237a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="hub") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("hub", "A") .add_edge("hub", "B") .add_edge("hub", "C") ) graph.alpha_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.05) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {3: 0.24849413982758015, 1: 0.2545175805172595, 4: 0.24849413982758015, 2: 0.24849413982758015} ``` ::: ::: ::: {#23a683bd .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.alpha_centrality(return_dict=True, alpha=0.5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {3: 0.23870593952832966, 1: 0.2838821814150109, 4: 0.23870593952832966, 2: 0.23870593952832966} ``` ::: ::: Storing the result as a node attribute lets it chain directly into visualization methods like `colorize_node_attrs()`: ::: {#f8834850 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="hub") .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="hub", target="A") .add_edge(source="hub", target="B") .add_edge(source="hub", target="C") ) ( graph .alpha_centrality(attr_name="alpha_cent") .colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="alpha_cent", node_attr_to="fillcolor") .describe() ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 4 Number of edges : 3 Directed : False Density : 0.50 Average degree (min, max) : 1.50 (1, 3) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True Computations on nodes: - alpha_centrality() -> attr: 'alpha_cent' (4 of 4 nodes) Node aesthetics: - fillcolor <- alpha_cent via colorize (palette: "default") (values: #1f77b4, #ff7f0e, 4 of 4 nodes) ``` ::: :::
